page.title: Virtual and Hybrid Event Platform Selection Guide
page.description: Compare platform types, cost models, production needs and timelines to choose the right virtual or hybrid event platform for your format and audience.
page.h1: How to choose a virtual and hybrid event platform
page.definition: A virtual and hybrid event platform is software that hosts live online or blended in-person and remote experiences, handling streaming, registration, engagement tools and analytics for webinars, summits and conferences.
page.quick_answer: Match the platform tier to your format: self-serve studios for webinars, enterprise suites for multi-track hybrids. Lock the platform and venue AV six to eight weeks out, then assign a producer to own the run of show and backup stream.

sections.h2: Which platform type matches your format and audience size?

blocks.p: Self-serve streaming studios suit single-track webinars up to a few hundred attendees; enterprise event suites handle multi-track agendas, expo booths and hybrid venue integration for thousands.

ul: Self-serve studios: StreamYard, Livestorm, Restream for simple webinars and town halls
Mid-tier event platforms: Zoom Events, Goldcast, Hopin for series and multi-session days
Enterprise suites: ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, Splash for large conferences, hybrid productions and deep CRM integration

sections.h2: How do the three cost models compare for your budget?

blocks.p: Three cost models dominate: per-host licences sized by attendee capacity, self-serve monthly plans, and annual contracts quoted by sales.

sections.h2: What production roles do you need beyond the software?

blocks.p: The platform is not the production; someone must own the run of show, rehearse speakers and keep a backup stream ready.

ul: Simple webinar: one producer manages run of show, speaker cues, Q&A and recording
Summit or online conference: show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator
Hybrid event: add venue AV liaison, camera operator and encoder technician for the in-room feed

sections.h2: What timeline and rehearsals does a hybrid event require?

blocks.p: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final.

ol: Week one to two: intake, brief, platform and venue AV contracts signed
Week three to four: speaker briefs, branded slide templates and lower thirds delivered
Week five: full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before live date
Day of: technical check sixty minutes before go-live, backup stream verified
Post-event: replay sent within twenty-four to forty-eight hours

sections.h2: How do you evaluate self-serve studios against enterprise suites?

blocks.p: Ten platforms compared below, from self-serve streaming studios to enterprise event suites; the choice turns on format complexity, integration needs and internal production capacity.

ul: Self-serve: fast setup, low admin, limited branding and no native registration or CRM sync
Mid-tier: built-in registration, networking lounges and analytics dashboards
Enterprise: single sign-on, multi-language, expo modules, dedicated success manager and SLA

faq.q: What is the typical production cost for a moderated webinar?
faq.a: Moderated webinars range from $2,500 to $7,500 per production based on West Peek Productions published range; this covers producer, rehearsal, branded assets, live Q&A, backup stream and edited recording.

faq.q: How much lead time does a hybrid summit need?
faq.a: A hybrid summit needs six to eight weeks of management; lock the platform and venue AV first, then build the run of show, speaker briefs and rehearsal schedule.

faq.q: Can we use our existing Zoom or Teams licence for a produced event?
faq.a: Yes, West Peek Productions produces events on the platform you already use, such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard, and supplies the crew, run of show and backup stream.

faq.q: What deliverables come with a produced virtual event?
faq.a: Deliverables include run of show, speaker brief and rehearsal, branded slide template and lower thirds, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, edited recording and social clips.

faq.q: Does West Peek Productions sell event platform licences?
faq.a: West Peek Productions does not sell event software; it produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events on the platform you choose and can help you evaluate options before you commit.
